title: Understanding the Cognitive Immersion of Hospitality Architecture in Culture and Nature: Cultural Psychology and Neuroscience Views
research_question: How does the aesthetic dimension of hospitality architecture impact human cognition, and what are the neurological underpinnings of cultural heritage and natural biodiversity reproduced in hotel architecture, as interpreted through the aesthetic triad?

participants.description: Three adult interviewees (1 undergraduate student majoring in architecture, 1 PhD candidate, 1 tourism blogger) from Hangzhou, China and Hong Kong, aged 24-30.
participants.recruitment: Interviewees were selected during a field survey conducted by a team of six researchers who visited and experienced the Amanfayun hotel for 3 days. The interviewees were hotel guests or passersby encountered during the survey.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Amanfayun, a luxury hotel in Hangzhou, China, known for its integration of cultural and natural elements in its architecture and landscape. The hotel's design includes U-shaped twin towers, strip-shaped sunshades, atrium space with plants, sloping roofs, and yellow earth walls, situated near Lingyin Temple and Zhejiang Buddhist College.
stimuli_or_exposures.source: Sample Selection: The Luxury Amanfayun Hotel in Hangzhou, China section, Figures 2 and 3

measures.construct: Aesthetic appreciation of hotel architecture and space
Perceived fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns of architecture
Influence of familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background on aesthetic knowledge and meaning

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (fluency, complexity, naturalistic patterns)
findings.mechanism: Achieved through the sensory-motor systems, which process visual and non-visual cues like luminance, color, motion, odor, sound, and temperature, and coordinate motor responses.
findings.quote: This study demonstrates that the evaluation of fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns of an architectural masterpiece can be achieved through the sensory-motor systems.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (familiarity, expectations, context, cultural background)
findings.consequent: Aesthetic knowledge of an individual and the meaning of architectural work
findings.mechanism: Past experiences in a cultural setting directly modulate present interactions and interpretations, engaging cognitive maps and building familiarity.
findings.quote: Our results also prove that familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background directly affect the aesthetic knowledge of an individual and the meaning of architectural work.

findings.antecedent: Interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements (from P1 and P2)
findings.mechanism: The emotion valuation system functions as a regulator to balance feelings and emotions generated by architectural aesthetics, avoiding excesses.
findings.quote: Moreover, the interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements is uniformly moderated by the emotion valuation system, resulting in a balanced appreciation of aesthetic architecture.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (sloping roofs, blocks in different colors/directions/heights)
findings.mechanism: Moderate complexity with harmonious unity and logical hierarchy in design levels.
findings.quote: For all the complexity, the sloping rooves of blocks in different directions, heights, and colors (Figure 2B) show the design hierarchy. All the buildings of Amanfayun are unified in texture and style, giving the hotel a harmonious appearance.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (hidden in woods, natural design elements like bonsai and rocky storages)
findings.consequent: Evocation of a 'dream temple' and traditional Chinese aesthetic
findings.mechanism: Organic design eliciting human affinity for natural features and processes, conferring psychological benefits.
findings.quote: Regarding naturalistic patterns, the building is hidden in woods, as shown in Figure 2C, with a dream temple inside. There are also natural design elements that have a traditional Chinese aesthetic, such as bonsai and rocky storages.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun hotel architecture (proximity to Lingyin Temple and Zhejiang Buddhist College, yellow earth walls)
findings.consequent: Echoing of local cultural and religious buildings, reflecting Buddhist serenity
findings.mechanism: Cultural context and meaning affect aesthetic experience, with the environment reflecting local cultural heritage.
findings.quote: As for context and cultural meaning, Amanfayun is close to Lingyin Temple, a famous Buddhist temple with almost 1,700 years of history, and Zhejiang Buddhist College. Therefore, the architecture and landscape of Amanfayun echo the buildings in the temple and the college, as shown in Figure 3B.

findings.antecedent: Amanfayun indoor suites (modified curtains, lamps, retro-look electric appliances, inconspicuous modern appliances)
findings.consequent: Guest satisfaction with elegance and comfort, ability to adjust indoor environment
findings.mechanism: Occupants' ability to control environmental parameters (like temperature) influences thermal comfort and overall satisfaction.
findings.quote: To satisfy the expectations of guests about controlling the environment, the indoor suites at Amanfayun were designed to combine elegance and comfort... There are modified curtains, lamps, and other electric appliances with a retro look for guests to adjust to the indoor environment.

findings.antecedent: Culture and nature (integrated into hospitality architecture)
findings.mechanism: Nature provides restorative value, refreshing the emotion valuation system and allowing for recovery from directed attention fatigue.
findings.quote: Finally, the study reveals the central roles of culture and nature in cognitive rejuvenation.

mechanisms: The aesthetic triad (sensory-motor, knowledge-meaning, and emotion valuation systems) provides a general neural model for architectural aesthetic experience.
Sensory-motor systems evaluate fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns through visual and non-visual cues, coordinating motor responses.
Knowledge-meaning systems are influenced by familiarity, expectations, context, and cultural background, shaping aesthetic knowledge and meaning based on past experiences and cognitive maps.
Emotion valuation systems regulate and balance feelings and emotions generated by architectural aesthetics, moderating the interaction between sensory-motor and knowledge elements.
Exposure to nature and cultural heritage provides cognitive rejuvenation by reducing stress (SRT) and restoring directed attention (ART).
implementation_implications: Hotel architectural design should integrate cultural and natural elements to positively impact consumer hospitality experiences and cognitive well-being.
Architectural designs should consider fluency, complexity, and naturalistic patterns to enhance sensory-motor appreciation.
Designs should incorporate elements that foster familiarity, meet expectations, provide relevant context, and reflect cultural meaning to enhance knowledge-meaning systems.
The interaction of sensory-motor and knowledge elements should be balanced by considering emotional valuation, aiming for a holistic and positive aesthetic experience.
Prioritizing culture and nature in design can contribute to cognitive rejuvenation and mental health benefits for occupants.

tables.description: Interview data overview, including job, gender, age, and domicile of the three participants.

limitations: The study employed a single-case research design with a very small sample size (3 interviewees), which limits the generalizability of the findings.
The qualitative nature of the data (in-depth interviews) provides rich insights but lacks quantitative measures for statistical significance and effect sizes.

paper_metadata.title: Cognitive representations of spatial location
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Spatial memory has fascinated psychologists ever since the discipline began, but a series of findings beginning in the middle of last century propelled its study into the domain of neuroscience and helped bring about the cognitive revolution in psychology. Starting with the discovery that the hippocampus plays a central role in memory, particularly spatial memory, studies of the mammalian hippocampus and related regions over the latter half of the century slowly uncovered an extensive neural system involved in processing place, head direction, objects, speed and other spatially informative parameters. Meanwhile, the concurrent discovery of hippocampal synaptic plasticity allowed theoreticians and experimentalists to collaborate in linking spatial perception and memory, and genetic techniques developed towards the end of the century opened the door to circuit dissections of these processes. Building on these discoveries, spatial cognition and episodic memory may be the first cognitive competences understood across all levels from molecules to behaviour.

crossref_authors.name: Kate J. Jeffery
crossref_authors.affiliation: Institute of Behavioural Neuroscience and Division of Psychology and Language Sciences, University College London, London, UK
